title: Work and study
job: Explain what you do all day, and how
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE INSTRUMENTAL OPENS HERE — the fifth case, and the last one this ladder needs for a while. Its endings are regular enough to state in one line: -om on a masculine or neuter noun (inzhenérom, spórtom), -oy on a feminine one or on any noun ending in -a (kollégoy, rabótoy), -im on the adjective in front of it (rússkim yazykóm). When the ending is the stressed syllable it is written -óm, as in vrachóm.

THERE IS NO WORD FOR "AS". Ya rabótayu inzhenérom is "I work as an engineer", and the whole of the "as" is the -om on the end. An English speaker reaches for kak, and kak inzhenér is a real Russian phrase meaning something else — "the way an engineer would". The case does the job a preposition does in English, which is the single loudest thing in this module.

s + INSTRUMENTAL is "together with": s kollégoy, s drúgom. The preposition is exactly what an English speaker expects and the ENDING is what they forget, so the two are learned as one thing. s never appears with a plain nominative — if you can say "with" in English, the Russian noun after it has to change shape.

s grows a vowel before an awkward cluster: so mnoy, not s mnoy. It is the same preposition with a syllable added so the mouth can get through it, and Russian does the same with v/vo and k/ko. Hearing so and filing it as a new word is the only mistake available here.

zanimát'sya TAKES THE INSTRUMENTAL WITH NO PREPOSITION AT ALL: zanimáyus' spórtom, zanimáyus' rússkim yazykóm. It is "I occupy myself with X", and the "with" is again inside the ending. Putting s in front of it changes the meaning to doing the activity in someone's company. Note also that it is L3-M1's -sya particle doing ordinary work — the row for that shape is there, not here.

Three verbs, three jobs, and they do not overlap: rabótayu is what you are paid for, uchús' is where you are enrolled, zanimáyus' is what you occupy yourself with. All three stay present and imperfective throughout this module — it is L1-M4's habitual grown up, not a new tense.

sentences.cue: I work as an engineer in Moscow

words.note: The plain form is inzhenér; the -om ending IS the English "as". You would use inzhenér to say what someone is, and inzhenérom to say what they do for a living.

sentences.trap: There is no word for "as" that you have forgotten — the ending carries all of it. Reaching for kak produces a comparison instead of a job.
sentences.sound: ya ra-BO-ta-yu in-zhy-NYE-ram v mask-VYE. The -om is unstressed and reduces to -am, so what you hear is the stem plus a swallowed syllable.

variations.cue: I work as a doctor in Moscow
variations.changed: a different profession

variations.cue: I work as an engineer from home
variations.changed: where, rather than what

mistake.why: kak turns it into a comparison — working the way an engineer works. The job itself takes the instrumental: Ya rabótayu inzhenérom.

sentences.usage: Answering what you do for a living.

sentences.cue: My sister works as a doctor

words.note: L2-M8's vrach in the instrumental. After the hushing ch the ending is written -om, and here it is the stressed syllable, so the stress moves off the stem.

sentences.trap: vrach has no everyday feminine form: a woman is a vrach and works vrachóm. Nothing in the profession word says she — only sestrá does.
sentences.sound: ma-YA ses-TRA ra-BO-ta-yet vra-CHOM. vrachóm is stressed on the ending, unlike inzhenérom, so the two do not rhyme.

variations.cue: My brother works as a doctor
variations.changed: a brother instead of a sister

variations.cue: My sister works as an engineer
variations.changed: a different profession

mistake.why: The nominative names what she IS; the job she works takes the instrumental. Moyá sestrá rabótayet vrachóm.

sentences.usage: Saying what somebody in your family does.
sentences.mnemonic: vrach becomes vrachóm, and the stress moves with it.

sentences.display: Ya rabótayu s kollégoy, a inogdá s drúgom
sentences.script: Я работаю с коллегой, а иногда с другом
sentences.cue: I work with a colleague, and sometimes with a friend
sentences.literal: I work with colleague-INSTR, and sometimes with friend-INSTR

words.note: "Together with", and it always takes the instrumental. It is a single letter said joined to the next word, so listen for it inside s-kollégoy rather than as a beat of its own.
The plain form kolléga ends in -a and means a man just as often as a woman. The -oy is the ending that -a demands, whoever the colleague is.
L2-M2's drug in the instrumental. A masculine noun takes -om and the stress stays where the nominative had it: drug, drúga, drúgom.

sentences.trap: kolléga looks feminine and is not. The ending you put on it follows the -a it ends in, not the person it names.
sentences.sound: ya ra-BO-ta-yu s ka-LYE-gay, a i-nag-DA s DRU-gam. Both endings are unstressed, which is exactly why they get dropped.

variations.display: Ya rabótayu s kollégoy kázhdyy den'
variations.script: Я работаю с коллегой каждый день
variations.cue: I work with a colleague every day
variations.changed: every day, and the friend dropped

variations.cue: I rarely work with a friend
variations.changed: rarely, and only the friend

mistake.display: Ya rabótayu s kolléga, a inogdá s drug
mistake.script: Я работаю с коллега, а иногда с друг
mistake.why: s never leaves the noun in its plain form: Ya rabótayu s kollégoy, a inogdá s drúgom.

sentences.usage: Describing who you sit beside at work.
sentences.mnemonic: s always brings an ending with it.

words.note: The person in charge of a department or a shift. It is neutral in tone: no Russian hears it as "chief" or as a complaint, and it is what you would say to their face.

sentences.trap: No verb, and none is missing. Russian's present tense of "to be" is silence, which the ladder has relied on since L1-M1.
sentences.sound: moy na-CHAL-nik O-chen DO-bryy. The soft sign in -l'nik keeps the l light, close to the l in "million".

variations.cue: My boss works from home
variations.changed: what he does rather than what he is

variations.cue: My sister is very kind
variations.changed: a woman, so the adjective turns feminine

mistake.why: There is no "is" to insert — yest' is for having and existing, not for linking. Moy nachál'nik óchen' dóbryy.

sentences.usage: Describing the people you work under.

words.cue: I study · I am a student
words.note: It names WHERE you are enrolled, never what subject. Another -s' verb — L3-M1's particle, doing the same job of marking a verb that takes no object.
The plain form is universitét; the -e is the prepositional after v, the case L1-M7 taught on kómnate. The word itself transfers whole from English.

sentences.trap: uchús' cannot take the subject as an object. "I study Russian" needs zanimáyus' and the instrumental, or a different verb entirely.
sentences.sound: ya u-CHUS v u-ni-vyer-si-TYE-tye. The stress in universitéte sits on the -té-, two syllables from the end.

variations.cue: I study and I work
variations.changed: two verbs, and no place named

variations.cue: Sometimes I study at home
variations.changed: sometimes, and at home

mistake.why: Without the particle the verb means "I teach", which is the opposite claim. Ya uchús' v universitéte.

sentences.usage: Saying what you are enrolled in.

sentences.cue: I do sport in the evening

words.cue: I do · I occupy myself with
words.note: "I occupy myself with" — and what you occupy yourself with goes straight into the instrumental with no preposition, exactly as a profession does after rabótayu.
The plain form sport is the borrowed English word, unchanged. The -om is the same ending inzhenérom takes, and it is unstressed here.

sentences.trap: No s in front of it. s means "in the company of a person"; the instrumental after zanimáyus' is what the activity actually IS.
sentences.sound: ya za-ni-MA-yus SPOR-tam VYE-cha-ram. Three words, and each one loses its final vowel to reduction.

variations.cue: I often do sport
variations.changed: often, and no time of day

variations.cue: I never do sport
variations.changed: never, with its obligatory ne

mistake.why: zanimát'sya needs no preposition at all: Ya zanimáyus' spórtom vécherom.

sentences.usage: Saying what you do after work.
sentences.mnemonic: Occupy yourself WITH — and say no "with".

words.note: L1-M1's rússkiy in the instrumental. The adjective takes -im and the noun takes -om, and they must agree: an adjective never keeps its plain form beside a changed noun.
L1-M4's yazýk in the instrumental. The stress moves onto the ending, so it is written -óm, exactly as it is in vrachóm.

sentences.trap: Both halves change. Russian never puts a case on the noun and leaves the adjective in front of it alone.
sentences.sound: ya za-ni-MA-yus RUS-kim ya-zy-KOM DO-ma. The two instrumentals end differently — -im then -óm — and only the second is stressed.

variations.cue: In the evening I study Russian
variations.changed: in the evening rather than at home

variations.cue: I rarely study Russian
variations.changed: rarely, and no place

mistake.why: Both words go into the instrumental together: Ya zanimáyus' rússkim yazykóm dóma.

sentences.usage: Telling a Russian speaker how you are learning.
sentences.mnemonic: The adjective follows its noun's case.

sentences.cue: My salary is not very big

words.note: One word squeezed out of "wage payment", and the everyday one. A Russian says zarpláta where an English speaker picks between pay, salary and wages.

sentences.trap: ne stands in front of what it denies. There is no verb here for it to attach to, so it denies óchen' bol'sháya and that is the whole negation.
sentences.sound: ma-YA zar-PLA-ta nye O-chen bal-SHA-ya. ne is unstressed and leans on the word after it, almost as one word.

variations.cue: My salary is very big
variations.changed: the negative dropped

variations.cue: My salary is not big
variations.changed: very removed, so the claim gets blunter

mistake.why: zarpláta ends in -a and is feminine, so everything around it must agree. Moyá zarpláta ne óchen' bol'sháya.

sentences.usage: Deflecting a question about money without a number.
sentences.mnemonic: One word for all of pay.

words.note: A work meeting with an agenda. Meeting a friend is L2-M6's vstrétimsya, and the two never swap: no Russian has a soveshchániye in a café.

sentences.trap: u menyá is L1-M8's "I have", doing the same job with a diary entry instead of a possession. There is still no verb for having.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra u me-NYA sa-vye-SHCHA-ni-ye. The shch is one long soft sound, not a sh followed by a ch.

variations.display: Závtra u menyá soveshchániye v Moskvé
variations.script: Завтра у меня совещание в Москве
variations.cue: Tomorrow I have a meeting in Moscow
variations.changed: where the meeting is

variations.cue: Today I have a meeting
variations.changed: today instead of tomorrow

mistake.why: Russian has no everyday verb for having, and imét' sounds like a form. Závtra u menyá soveshchániye.

sentences.usage: Turning down an invitation by naming what is in the diary.
sentences.mnemonic: A meeting is AT you, not had by you.

sentences.cue: Would you like to work with me?

words.note: s with a vowel added so the mouth can manage the next word: so mnoy, never s mnoy. It is the same preposition, and Russian does the same with v/vo and k/ko.
The instrumental of ya. Every pronoun has one, and this is the one to learn first because so mnoy is said constantly.

sentences.trap: s mnoy is unsayable rather than merely wrong, and a learner who has only met s will build it. The extra o is not a second word to memorise.
sentences.sound: vy kha-TI-tye ra-BO-tat sa MNOY. so is unstressed and reduces to sa, so the pair sounds like one word, sa-MNOY.

variations.cue: Do you want to work with me?
variations.changed: ty, to someone you already know well

variations.cue: Would you like to work with a colleague?
variations.changed: with a colleague, so plain s comes back

mistake.why: Before mnoy the preposition grows its vowel: Vy khotíte rabótat' so mnoy?

sentences.usage: Proposing a project to someone at work you address as vy.
sentences.mnemonic: so mnoy, always with the o.
